subject: Archaeology
title: Community Archaeology: Digging Together
description: A 60-second lesson on Community Archaeology: Digging Together.

hook.text: Archaeology used to be done by experts who told locals what their heritage meant. Now communities dig their own stories.

buildup.text: Community archaeology invites local people to participate in excavations, record oral histories.

discovery.text: In the UK, the BBC's 'Time Team' inspired millions. Community digs surged, and volunteers found thousands of new sites.

twist.text: In Australia, Aboriginal communities now lead excavations on their own land — reversing a century of outsider-driven.

climax.text: Citizen science platforms let anyone analyze satellite images, transcribe old records, or classify pottery from home.

punchline.text: The past belongs to everyone. Archaeology is finally starting to act like it.

quiz.question: What is community archaeology?
options: Hiring local labor to do excavation work at reduced cost
Inviting local people to participate, record oral histories, and interpret their own past
Training community members to become professional archaeologists
